svg.title: Figure 2
svg.desc: Figure 2. The flag's disc against the computed sky. Filled stars: the 27 stars as placed in Annex 2 of Law 8.421/1992. Open circles: where a mirrored, zenith-centred stereographic projection of the sky at 08:30 local mean time on 15 November 1889, at Rio de Janeiro, puts the same stars after the best similarity fit. Lines join each star to its computed place. Dashed: the ecliptic; dotted: the celestial equator, under the same fit.

rdf:Description.dc:creator: Rodrigo Jazinski
rdf:Description.dc:source: Jazinski, R. (2026). Composed, not observed: What the celestial disc of the Brazilian flag carries of the sky over Rio de Janeiro on 15 November 1889, and what its texts supply (Working paper, version 0.0.7). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24480292

svg.text: Star as drawn (Annex 2, Law 8.421/1992), sized by class
Computed place, 08:30 LMT, 15 Nov 1889, Rio; mirrored, best fit
Disc radius 3.5 modules. Data: flagsky_stars_v0_0_7.csv; script sky_1889.py (both deposited with the paper).
